modelNote: Hover any box or arrow for a plain-language explanation. Dashed arrows are out-of-band (build/push, shared-disk writes); solid arrows are live HTTPS traffic. Nothing here runs on a personal machine — the live system is three containers on the WikiCafe server plus each person's browser.

nodes.note: Marc's laptop. Its ONLY job is to build the two Docker images and push them to the registry. It is never in the running path — switch it off and the live SODOTO system on WikiCafe keeps working. Not a server; not something users ever touch.
nodes.label:
Marc's dev machine
(build only — not in runtime path)

nodes.note: GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) — a public library of ready-to-run software images hosted by GitHub at ghcr.io. Marc pushes the built images here; the WikiCafe server pulls them from here to run. Think of it as the shelf a packaged app sits on between 'built' and 'running'.
nodes.label:
GitHub Container Registry
ghcr.io/marpie1/*

nodes.note: Caddy — a small web server at the front door of the WikiCafe machine. It handles HTTPS (automatically getting and renewing the TLS certificate from Let's Encrypt, so the padlock works) and routes each web address to the right container behind it. Nothing SODOTO-specific — just secure traffic and routing.
nodes.label:
Caddy — HTTPS / TLS
(WikiCafe server)

nodes.note: sofi-proxy — a small Python web server running as a container. Two jobs: (1) serves the browser tools such as the issuer tool, and (2) writes finished badges into the wiki on the browser's behalf, since a web page can't write wiki files directly. The trusted middleman for writes. Reached at sodoto.ndcgroup…
nodes.label:
sofi-proxy
issuer tool + wiki writes
(WikiCafe)

nodes.note: FedWiki — the wiki server, running as a container. It hosts and serves the learner portfolio pages and the badge ledger, and renders each badge with the sodoto-badge plugin, including the client-side Verify button. Reached at wiki-sodoto.ndcgroup…
nodes.label:
FedWiki
portfolios + badge ledger
(WikiCafe)

nodes.note: The coordinator's own web browser, on their own computer. They open the issuer tool over HTTPS, run the See / Do / Teach workflow, and paste the NDC's private key to sign the badge. Signing happens right here in the browser — the key never goes to the server.
nodes.label:
Coordinator browser
opens issuer tool · signs Ed25519

nodes.note: Any web browser, anywhere. It opens a learner's portfolio page on the wiki and clicks Verify. The signature check runs entirely in that browser, from the badge's DID — no login, no account, no server call. This is what makes a credential verifiable by anyone, forever.
nodes.label:
Learner / verifier browser
views portfolio · verifies badge

edges.note: Done by Marc at development time, not live traffic. He builds the two images and uploads them to the registry. Dashed = out-of-band, not part of the running system.
edges.label: build & push images

edges.note: The WikiCafe server downloads the sofi-proxy image from the registry so it can run it. Happens at deploy/update time, not on every visit.
edges.label: image pulled

edges.note: The WikiCafe server downloads the FedWiki image from the registry so it can run it — same pull, other container.
edges.label: image pulled

edges.note: The coordinator's browser reaches the issuer tool over secure HTTPS at sodoto.ndcgroup… Caddy answers at the front door and passes it inward.
edges.label: HTTPS  sodoto.ndcgroup…

edges.note: The learner/verifier's browser reaches the portfolios over secure HTTPS at wiki-sodoto.ndcgroup… Caddy answers at the front door and passes it inward.
edges.label: HTTPS  wiki-sodoto.ndcgroup…

edges.note: Inside the server, Caddy forwards requests for sodoto.ndcgroup… to the sofi-proxy container, which listens on port 8765.
edges.label: reverse proxy :8765

edges.note: Inside the server, Caddy forwards requests for wiki-sodoto.ndcgroup… to the FedWiki container, which listens on port 3000.
edges.label: reverse proxy :3000

edges.note: The two containers share one folder on the server's disk (a Docker 'volume'). sofi-proxy writes a badge there as a page file; FedWiki serves that same file. That shared folder is how a write becomes visible on the portfolio. Dashed = filesystem sharing, not network traffic.
edges.label: writes pages (shared volume)
